newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaireans fleeing heavy fighting report cholera.
newsitem.headline: Zaireans fleeing heavy fighting report cholera.

text.p: Some 800 Zaireans reached the eastern Zairean city of Goma by boat on Thursday and many reported cholera and heavy battles between rebel and Hutu forces to the west.
Zairean Lwaboshi Menne quoted members of the exiled Rwandan Hutu Interahamwe militia as saying they would fight foreign troops in a multinational force being sent to eastern Zaire.

"If foreign troops come here the Interahamwe are saying they will fight them before they run," said Menne, adding the fleeing Zaireans were blocked from taking the lakeside road from Sake back to Goma city by heavily armed Rwandan Hutu militiamen.
"They were everywhere...on the roads and in the bush," he said.
The Interahamwe and former Rwandan Hutu troops led the 1994 genocide of up to a million Tutsis and Hutu moderates before fleeing to Zaire with 1.1 million refugees in fear of reprisals.

Rebels say the Interahamwe and former Rwandan Armed Forces (FAR) are holding refugees as human shields in Mugunga camp, 10 km (six miles) west of Goma. Heavy fighting broke out around the camp on Thursday.

The United States and other contributing nations to the force have said their forces will not disarm militiamen, a step aid workers say is essential to prompt a mass exodus home by the refugees as demanded by the governments of Rwanda and Zaire.

The Zaireans, who reached Goma by boats on Lake Kivu, said they had left Goma as rebel forces closed in two weeks ago and headed through Mugunga to Sake, six km (four miles) west of the camp, which was the world's largest with some 400,000 refugees.
"We left Sake because there is a lot of fighting between Zairean rebels, the Interahamwe and the Mai-Mai (a Zairean tribal militia)," said Lolonga Osakamu, 28, in rebel-held Goma.
"We tried to return to Goma via Mugunga but we were blocked on the road by the Interahamwe. The Interahamwe have extended their line outwards from Mugunga to the village of Ndosho.
"They are heavily armed. They have blocked the road and I saw them making defensive positions. We returned to Sake but there is illness in Sake and many people have cholera," he added.
"I only arrived here now with my very small brother," said Kamat Kakul.
"There were 18 members of my family in Sake. We are the only two left. All the others are dead or lost. Three of them died because they were ill. Some were shot and the rest fled," he said.

"We've come back by boat because the road at Mugunga is blocked by Rwandan Hutus who looted everything we had and said they would kill us. There are a lot of ill people the other side of Sake where there is fighting with the rebels," Kakul added.

French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette said on Thursday France hoped the first troops in a multinational force would be in Zaire by the weekend and their mission would be limited to giving aid to 1.2 million Rwandan and Burundian refugees.
